articles.title: Sonay Kartal: New British number one makes rapid rise after a slow recovery from back injury
articles.summary: Six months ago, Sonay Kartal could not brush her teeth without "being in agony" - now she's the British number one after three events back from a long-term back injury.
articles.body:
Six months ago, Sonay Kartal could not stand up and brush her teeth without "being in agony".

The pain caused by a stress fracture in her back eventually subsided, but the 24-year-old Briton still had a long road to full recovery, which needed to be navigated with patience and hard work.

Kartal did not make her return to competitive action until little under a month ago.

But on Monday, she became the new British number one after an extraordinary week at the Wuhan Open, where she reached the biggest final of her career in just her third tournament back.

"In the first month or so, I was at home in bed - sometimes I had good days but there were also bad days where I wasn't really able to walk without some form of pain," Kartal said.

"It was a slow process and it makes you think you do take every day things for granted a bit."

Given where Kartal was six months ago, and the length of time she was out injured, reaching the Wuhan final cannot be overstated as an achievement.

As a WTA 1,000 event, it is in the tier of tournaments directly below the Grand Slams and attracts the strongest fields on the women's tour.

Kartal knocked out a series of opponents with considerable pedigree - including current top-10 players and former Grand Slam champions - before running out of steam against this year's French Open runner-up Maja Chwalinska.

Falling to a brutal defeat from a set and break up in the final will undoubtedly sting. Kartal, though, quickly acknowledged the bigger picture is already more positive than she could have predicted.

Kartal was ranked 54th in the world when the back issue struck at Indian Wells in March and she used a protected injury ranking - given to players who have been out for six months or more - to compete in Wuhan.

Earning 650 points as the runner-up saw Kartal's ranking rocket from 170th to 49th - and now closing in on a career-high of 44th achieved in July 2025 after reaching the last 16 at Wimbledon.

And it is an example of the WTA's special ranking rule working as it is intended: providing a fair platform for a player to re-establish her position after a prolonged and unavoidable absence.

Regaining her ranking just 10 matches into her comeback will have real significance for the 2027 season.

Kartal will no longer need to use a protected ranking to enter tournaments including the Australian Open, meaning she can have greater choice over when and where to play as she continues to manage her workload.

On Monday, she pulled out of the Japan Open in Osaka, where she was due to play her first-round match on Tuesday.

"My goal on the Asian swing was just to try to defend those points I had from last year and make the use of the protected ranking worthwhile," said Kartal, who also won two matches at the China Open in Beijing.

"I think I've gone above and beyond that. The goal has been achieved this week and I'm in a good spot for the rest of the year and next year."

Kartal's re-emergence is timely too when considering the bigger picture of British success at the highest level.

With Kartal absent from three of the four majors, no British women went past the second round of a Grand Slam tournament in 2026.

Kartal has only managed to do that twice in her career - reaching the third round at Wimbledon in 2024 and going one stage further last year - but showed in Wuhan she has the ability to thrive at elite level.

She became the first British player to reach a WTA 1000 final since Johanna Konta in 2019 and, despite losing to 22nd-ranked Chwalinska, still recorded the best result by a British woman since Emma Raducanu won the US Open title in 2021.

Alongside Arthur Fery's extraordinary run to the Wimbledon semi-finals in the summer, it is a much-needed bright spot for the nation's tennis fans.

Similarly to Fery, she is not blessed with the height and power which many of the leading players on both tours are genetically given, but she certainly has enough damaging tools which can help anchor her inside the top 50.

In Wuhan, her consistent hitting from the baseline, supreme athleticism and level-headedness were the keys to her success.

Staying fit over the coming months will be another important factor.

Kartal says the stress fracture in her back has completely healed and her team say she "worked her socks off, 9-5 all the time" during rehabilitation to ensure she could hit the ground running when she did return.

It was telling that Kartal quickly paid tribute to her coach Ben Reeves, fitness coach Ian Aylward and physio Dani Gillanders after collecting the runners-up trophy.

"If it wasn't for them I wouldn't be here," Kartal said.

"It makes it even better that the three people who helped me get back to fitness and fixed my back are with me. It's been a special week for all of us."

articles.title: Rafa Jódar se sitúa noveno del año y se acerca a las ATP Finals de Turín
articles.standfirst: El madrileño le saca 279 puntos a De Miñaur, que ahora mismo sería el primer reserva
articles.summary: El madrileño le saca 279 puntos a De Miñaur, que ahora mismo sería el primer reserva
articles.body: El tenis masculino español puede clasificar a dos españoles en las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22 de noviembre). A Carlos Alcaraz, que ya tiene el billete, se le puede unir su compatriota Rafa Jódar. El madrileño ha ganado dos posiciones, gracias a la final del Masters 1000 de Shanghái, y se sitúa este lunes noveno de la Race 2026. Los 3.159 puntos le dejan a 166 de la octava plaza, que ahora mismo ocupa Arthur Fils, y le distancian de Alex de Miñaur en 279 puntos. El australiano es hoy el primer reserva de la cita de maestros. Novak Djokovic se queda a 319 puntos del fenómeno de Leganés. Es por ello que ha aceptado una invitación para participar en el Open 500 de Basilea. Rafa y el serbio coincidirán en tierras suizas. Jódar se ha quedado a tan sólo 91 puntos de convertirse en el vigésimo miembro de la 'Armada' en ingresar en las diez primeras posiciones del ranking de entradas de la ATP. En el Open 500 de Basilea (26 de octubre al 1 de noviembre) volverá a tener la oportunidad de ser el tercer español más precoz en conseguirlo tras Rafa Nadal y Carlos Alcaraz. Alejandro Davidovich, flamante campeón de Shanghái, es hoy el decimocuarto tenista del año y se ha metido en la carrera por estar en Turín. Le separan 649 puntos y quedan por disputarse 1.500 (Basilea y el Masters 1000 de París).

articles.title: Svitolina anuncia su separación de Monfils: "Nuestro matrimonio termina, pero nuestra familia no"
articles.standfirst: La tenista ucraniana explica el impacto emocional de la guerra y agradece el apoyo del francés: "Nunca me soltó la mano"
articles.summary: La tenista ucraniana explica el impacto emocional de la guerra y agradece el apoyo del francés: "Nunca me soltó la mano"
articles.body: Elina Svitolina ha anunciado el final de su matrimonio con Gaël Monfils a través de un comunicado en Instagram en el que explica el difícil momento personal que atraviesa. La ucraniana habla del sufrimiento que le ha provocado la guerra en su país y de una decisión dolorosa: "Necesito reencontrarme conmigo misma y no puedo hacerlo dentro de nuestro matrimonio". "Esto es lo más difícil que he tenido que compartir", comienza el mensaje. Svitolina recuerda que el año pasado explicó que necesitaba alejarse de las pistas porque no se encontraba en condiciones emocionales de competir. Ahora ha querido contar qué había detrás: "Lo que no visteis fueron las noches sin dormir, las dudas y la sensación de estar perdiéndome poco a poco". La tenista destaca el apoyo de Monfils durante todo ese proceso. "Gaël lo vio todo. Nunca me soltó la mano. Luchamos juntos durante mucho tiempo, con todo lo que teníamos", explica. Pero también expresa los límites de esa ayuda: "Algunas batallas se libran en lo más profundo de una misma y ningún amor de otra persona puede ganarlas por ti". Svitolina asegura que comprender lo que necesitaba y trasladárselo a su marido ha sido especialmente duro. "Es la verdad más difícil que he tenido que afrontar y lo más difícil que he tenido que decirle a la persona que amo". Del francés destaca su respuesta: "Ha respetado lo que necesito con una fortaleza y una elegancia que nunca olvidaré". El comunicado está atravesado por el cariño y el agradecimiento hacia quien ha compartido sus mejores y peores momentos. "Gaël me ha querido en mis mayores alegrías y en mis momentos más oscuros, y yo lo he querido con todo mi corazón", escribe. Por encima de la separación queda su hija Skai, a quien sitúa en el centro de esta nueva etapa. "Skai siempre será lo primero. Nuestro matrimonio termina, pero nuestra familia no. Siempre seremos sus padres, juntos, en cada paso de su vida". Svitolina cierra el anuncio con una petición de respeto para ambos y sin señalar culpables: "Solo hay dos personas que se han querido profundamente y una historia que está cambiando de forma". Y solicita comprensión y privacidad: "Os pedimos amabilidad y el espacio que necesitamos para sanar".

articles.title: Elina Svitolina announces split from Gael Monfils: ‘Our marriage is ending, but our family is not’
articles.summary: Ukrainian tennis star Elina Svitolina has announced the end of her marriage to French tennis player Gael Monfils, describing the decision as the most
articles.body: Ukrainian tennis star Elina Svitolina has announced the end of her marriage to French tennis player Gael Monfils, describing the decision as the most difficult thing she has ever had to share and opening up about the emotional struggles that shaped her journey over the past year.The world No. 6 made the announcement in an emotional Instagram post on Monday, explaining that she needed to rediscover herself after battling the psychological toll of the war in Ukraine. The couple, who have a daughter, Skai, together, said their family would remain united despite the end of their marriage.“This is the most difficult thing I have ever had to share,” Svitolina wrote.The 32-year-old revealed that she had rarely spoken publicly about her inner struggles but had reached a point where she needed to step away from tennis to recover emotionally. She described sleepless nights, doubts and a feeling of losing herself during a particularly difficult period.‘No amount of love from someone else can win them for you’Svitolina acknowledged the role Monfils played in supporting her through her struggles, saying the Frenchman stood by her during some of the darkest moments of her life.“Gaël saw all of this. He never let go of my hand. We fought through it together for a long time, giving it all our strength,” she wrote.However, the Ukrainian explained that the emotional battles she was facing ultimately required a personal journey that she felt she could not undertake within their marriage.“But some battles happen deep inside you, and no amount of love from someone else can win them for you,” she wrote.“With time, I came to understand that I need to find my way back to myself and that I cannot do that within our marriage.”Svitolina described the decision as an extremely painful one, particularly because of the love and support she had shared with Monfils.“This is the hardest truth I have ever had to face and the hardest thing I have ever had to say to the person I love,” she said.She also paid tribute to Monfils for the way he responded to her decision, saying he had listened to her needs with dignity and understanding.“Gaël loved me in both the happiest and the darkest moments of my life. And I loved him with all my heart,” she added.Daughter Skai remains their priorityDespite confirming the end of their marriage, Svitolina stressed that their responsibilities as parents would remain unchanged. The couple share a daughter, Skai, who they said would continue to be their foremost priority.“Together, we built a beautiful life, and we were given the most precious gift of all, our daughter, Skai,” Svitolina wrote.“Skai will always come first. Our marriage is ending, but our family is not. We will always be her parents, side by side, at every step of her life.”The Ukrainian also made it clear that neither partner should be blamed for the separation, describing it as a difficult personal decision rather than the result of wrongdoing by either individual.“There are only two people who deeply loved each other, and a story that is now taking a different form,” she wrote, asking the public to respect their privacy as they navigate the transition.“We ask you to treat us with kindness and give us the privacy and time we need to heal. Thank you for your love.”Monfils' retirement adds another chapterThe announcement comes amid a significant transition in Monfils' tennis career. The 40-year-old Frenchman had planned to retire at the end of the 2026 season, with a farewell appearance at the Paris Masters expected to be a fitting conclusion in front of his home crowd.However, the sport’s drug-testing organisation has listed Monfils among players who have declared themselves retired, with his career officially ending on October 5.Monfils, a former world No. 6, enjoyed a long career marked by his athleticism and showmanship, while Svitolina has established herself among the leading players on the women’s tour.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Elina Svitolina announces 'difficult' separation from husband Gael Monfils after five years of marriage
articles.summary: Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils have announced their separation; The tennis players married in 2021 and have a four-year-old daughter; Watch the Japan Open all this week, live on Sky Sports Tennis
articles.body:
In an emotional Instagram post, the 32-year-old Ukrainian opened up about the mental toll of Russia's ongoing war against her country, describing sleepless nights and self-doubt.

Svitolina said she had come to realise she needed to rediscover herself and could no longer do so within her marriage. "This is the most difficult thing I have ever had to share," she wrote.

"Everyone knows how much Ukraine means to me. What I have rarely spoken about is what the war has done to me inside.

"With time, I came to understand that I need to find my way back to myself and that I cannot do that within our marriage.

"It is the hardest truth I have ever had to face and the hardest thing I have ever had to tell the person I love. Gael listened. He has respected what I need with a strength and grace I will never forget."

Svitolina - a four-time grand slam semi-finalist - and French former world No 6 Monfils, 40, married in 2021 and have a four-year-old daughter, Skai.

"Skai will always come first," Svitolina added. "Our marriage is ending, but our family is not.

"Please know that there is no one to blame here. There are only two people who loved each other deeply and a story that is changing shape."

Only a few months ago Svitolina and Monfils had joined forces to reach the semi-finals of the US Open Mixed Doubles Championship.

Svitolina and Monfils had impressed in the tournament until coming up against Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli in the last four.

More recently, Svitolina was in action at the Wuhun Open, but ran into an inspired Sonay Kartal, with the Brit winning their quarter-final clash in three sets.
